title: Microsoft Azure AI Engineer Associate
notes: Azure AI Engineers build, manage, and deploy AI solutions across the full lifecycle: requirements, design, development, deployment, integration, maintenance, performance tuning, and monitoring, collaborating with architects, data scientists/engineers, IoT, infra, and software devs.

Azure AI Foundry provides hubs and projects to organize resources, models, data connections, prompt flows, evaluations, and deployments; use it as the control plane for generative AI, language, vision, speech, search, and information extraction.

Choose services by scenario: Generative (Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models), NLP/Text analytics (Azure AI Language), Speech (Azure AI Speech), Computer Vision (Azure AI Vision, Custom Vision), Knowledge Mining (Azure AI Search), Information Extraction (Document Intelligence).

Responsible AI principles: fairness, reliability/safety, privacy/security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability; apply via Content Safety, filters/blocklists, prompt shields, RBAC, audit trails, and governance policies.
Authentication options: API (subscription) keys or Microsoft Entra ID; prefer managed identity for least-privilege, secretless auth; assign RBAC at resource scope.
Network security: use private endpoints and firewall rules to restrict to VNets or IP ranges; for internet-hosted apps, add specific public IPs to ‘Selected networks’ allowlist.
Key rotation and secret hygiene: avoid embedding secrets in code; prefer managed identity; if keys are used, store in Azure Key Vault and rotate regularly.

Monitoring and logging: enable metrics and diagnostics; use Application Insights, Azure Monitor, and model-level telemetry (latency, token usage, cost, throughput, error rates); set alerts and budgets.
Cost management: select right SKU, region, and quota; monitor usage; scale appropriately; power down unused resources; favor multi-service accounts where appropriate; cache and batch to reduce calls.

CI/CD: deploy AI resources and configurations via IaC (Bicep/ARM/Terraform) and pipelines (Azure DevOps/GitHub Actions); include tests, policy checks, and staged rollouts; version models and prompt flows.
Containerization: some services support containers (Vision, Language, DI); use for edge/local/offline scenarios; plan license/egress/telemetry; keep models updated.
Data storage patterns: Blob Storage for documents/images/audio/video; Azure Files for shared mounts; Cosmos DB/SQL for metadata; Data Lake for analytics; align with security, cost, and latency.
Multi-region and HA: plan for regional quotas and failover; replicate indexes and storage when required; confirm model availability per region.
RBAC roles to know: Cognitive Services User (invoke APIs), Contributor/Owner (manage), Reader (observe); Storage Blob Data Reader/Contributor for DI/Vision pipelines against Blob.

Content Safety integration best practices: set severity thresholds conservatively at first; log blocked cases; review false positives/negatives; fine-tune filters and blocklists; support appeal paths.
Governance framework: define risk taxonomy, review board, human-in-the-loop checkpoints for high-risk outputs, incident response, model inventory (owner, data lineage, eval results).
Azure OpenAI models: GPT-4-family (text, reasoning, multi‑modal variants), GPT‑3.5‑turbo, embeddings models, and DALL‑E for images; select based on capability, latency, cost, and context window.
Prompt message roles: system (persona, rules, formatting), user (request), assistant (history), tool/function messages; keep system message authoritative and concise; include guardrails and examples.
Generation controls: temperature (randomness), top_p (nucleus sampling), presence/frequency penalties (topic/duplication control), max_tokens (budget); tune per use case and track cost/quality.
Prompt patterns: few-shot exemplars, chain-of-thought (internal reasoning hidden), retrieval-augmented prompts with citations, output schema enforcement with JSON-mode/functions/tools.
Prompt Flow in Foundry: author multi-node flows (retrieval, grounding, LLM, post‑processors), evaluate runs with datasets, compare variants (A/B), capture traces, register best flow for deployment.
RAG architecture: ingest → chunk → embed → index → retrieve (k, hybrid, filters) → rerank → generate; log citations; cache retrievals; re-embed when data drifts or model upgrades.
Strictness parameter (On‑your‑data): increases relevance threshold so fewer low‑relevance docs are considered; balance precision vs recall with K (retrieved documents) and filters.
Vector search: store embeddings in Azure AI Search vector fields; choose cosine or dot‑product; combine with keyword/semantic (hybrid) for robust retrieval; consider vector sizes & storage costs.
Chunking strategy: choose chunk size and overlap based on genre (short FAQs vs long PDFs); smaller chunks improve precision but increase index size; store metadata (title, section, page).
Grounding data governance: keep sensitive data in secure stores; enforce per‑user filter contexts (e.g., ACL filters) so retrieval respects authorization; log queries and access.
Evaluation of genAI: automatic metrics (BLEU/ROUGE for summarization proxies), human‑in‑the‑loop ratings, guardrail tests (jailbreak, toxicity); regression tests in CI.
Image generation (DALL‑E): body must include ‘prompt’; for quality use ‘quality=hd’; control size (e.g., 1024x1792); n controls count; output format independent from quality.
Assistants: use tool-use and retrieval; constrain capabilities; set timeouts; stream tokens for UX; capture feedback for reinforcement; limit function/tool hallucinations via schema.
Agentic solutions: combine planning, tool-use, and memory to autonomously solve tasks; useful for workflows spanning retrieval, calls to APIs, and iterative reasoning.
Azure AI Foundry Agent Service: create agents tied to specific model deployments; configure tools (function calling, search connectors), memory, and security; monitor runs.
Semantic Kernel: orchestrate plugins (skills), planners, memories; compose workflows; supports C#/Python; good for multi-agent and tool integration patterns.
Autogen: agent-to-agent collaboration library; define roles (planner, coder, critic), safety boundaries, and termination conditions; record dialogues for audit.
Testing agents: seed with eval tasks, limit actions per run, set budget/time constraints, capture telemetry; add human approvals for high‑risk actions.
Azure AI Vision Image Analysis features: captioning/description, tagging, object detection, optical character recognition (OCR), face attributes (if enabled), adult/racy/gore flags, dominant colors.
Dominant background color outputs limited to a fixed set (e.g., black, blue, brown, gray, green, orange, pink, purple, red, teal, white, yellow).
Spatial Analysis: detect presence and movement of people in video streams; requires specific camera placement and supported regions/SKUs; consider privacy signage and consent.

Azure AI Video Indexer: upload → index → query; extract transcripts (customizable language model), scenes, topics, faces, and keyframes; to fetch keyframe thumbnails call: get index → get thumbnail by timestamp/keyframe id.
Custom Vision: choose classification vs object detection; tag consistently; split train/validation; evaluate precision/recall/mAP; publish best iteration; retrieve Prediction URL/key for production.
Custom Vision Compact domains: required for export to ONNX/CoreML/TensorFlow for mobile/edge; trade some accuracy for size/latency; design for offline operation.
Edge considerations: quantization, CPU/GPU/NPU support, batching, and thermal limits; schedule updates when connectivity returns; log predictions locally.
Azure AI Language Text Analytics: key phrase extraction (identify main topics), named entity recognition (people/locations/orgs), PII detection (names, addresses, SSNs), sentiment and opinion mining.
Question Answering: best for static knowledge with predictable answers; imports formatted text/URLs/lists; returns same answer for same question; multi-turn and chit‑chat supported.
Conversational Language Understanding (CLU): intents + entities; List entities (Strict) match only catalog phrases; Regex entities capture flexible patterns; retrain after labeling changes.
Evaluation metrics: Precision = TP/(TP+FP); Recall = TP/(TP+FN); F1 = harmonic mean(precision, recall); choose metric by business risk (false positives vs false negatives).
Azure AI Speech: batch and real-time STT; TTS with neural voices and SSML prosody; speaker identification (who in a group), text‑dependent/independent verification for auth use‑cases.
Batch transcription storage: Azure Storage is the default supported source; ensure SAS or managed identity access; specify container and output location.
Azure AI Translator: document and text translation; custom translator with parallel corpora; BLEU score 40–59 indicates high‑quality translation; evaluate per domain.

Azure AI Search index design: define key (unique id), searchable fields (full‑text), filterable/sortable/facetable flags per field; keep analyzers consistent with languages; store vectors for embeddings.
queryType: ‘full’ enables wildcards, regex, and fuzzy; ‘simple’ is limited; semantic search improves summaries/reranking; hybrid search combines keyword + vector signals.
Skillsets and indexers: define data sources (Blob, SQL, etc.), attach built‑in skills (OCR, entity recognition, language detection, key phrases, entity linking) or custom skills (Azure Functions).
Knowledge store projections: file/object/table projections capture enriched outputs for downstream analytics and validation.
Vector store operations: choose embedding model; track embedding dimension and version; schedule re-embedding on schema/model/data changes; consider HNSW parameters and memory footprint.
Facets and filters: use ‘facetable’ for category counts; combine with $filter to narrow; precompute common facets for speed; avoid excessive cardinality facets.
Document Intelligence models: Read (text), Layout (structure with tables/checkboxes/selection marks), Prebuilt (Invoice/Receipt/ID) for structured fields, and Custom models for bespoke forms.
Model selection guidance: Layout for structure‑preserving extraction across PDFs with tables/marks; Invoice for vendor invoices with totals/dates; Read for pure text extraction including handwriting.
Custom model training: label fields and tables; provide representative samples; split training/validation sets; compose models to route multiple form types through a single endpoint.
Input quality: prefer text‑based PDFs and high‑resolution images; ensure orientation/cropping; low‑resolution scans hurt OCR accuracy; normalize templates if possible.
Post‑processing: validate and normalize dates/currency; confidence thresholds and human review; push extracted data to databases/ERPs and index to Azure AI Search for retrieval.
Content Understanding: end‑to‑end ingestion for documents/images/audio/video with summarization, classification, and attribute extraction; chain with Search for RAG.

Threats to genAI apps: prompt injection, jailbreaks (role‑play, system‑rule overriding, encoded attacks), data exfiltration via tool use, sensitive info leakage; mitigate with Content Safety and robust system prompts.
Content Safety for images/text: classify at severity levels; tune block/allow lists; add pre‑ and post‑generation checks; label and log for audits; evaluate impact on false positives.

UPIA/Jailbreak risk detection: detect attempts to subvert rules; combine with input/output filtering; add refusal patterns and safe‑completion fallbacks; secure tool functions with parameter validation.

Performance tuning levers: cache RAG retrievals, reduce retrieved K with higher strictness, compress prompts, reuse conversation state, stream tokens, batch non‑interactive work, and select lower‑latency models where acceptable.
Diagnostics: collect traces (Prompt Flow), correlate user/session IDs, capture retrieval set and chosen citations; store anonymized datasets for offline evaluation.
Versioning: track model deployment name/version, prompt templates, embeddings model version, index schema; use semantic versioning and changelogs; rollback strategies ready.
Edge/container deployments: pin compatible model versions and dependencies; validate on target hardware; monitor telemetry locally and sync on reconnect.

Use Azure AI Vision Image Analysis to detect adult/racy content with minimal effort; use Custom Vision when you must train domain‑specific classifiers; use Spatial Analysis for real‑time people presence/movement.
Use Azure AI Video Indexer to extract insights from videos and customize speech models; fetch keyframes by first requesting the video index to learn IDs/timestamps.
Use Azure AI Language: key phrase extraction to identify concepts; PII detection to redact names/addresses; sentiment to gauge opinion; CLU for intents/entities; Question Answering for static FAQs.
Use Azure AI Search with ‘facetable’ fields for category counts, ‘queryType=full’ for wildcards; use semantic + vector hybrid for best relevance; enrich with built‑in Entity Linking to Wikipedia.
Use Document Intelligence Layout for structured extraction (text/tables/marks), Invoice for invoice fields, Read for text; train Custom models for bespoke forms; prefer text‑based PDFs for accuracy.
For generative apps on enterprise data, prefer RAG with Azure AI Search over fine‑tuning for lower cost and freshness; increase Strictness to filter noise; log citations for trust.
For authentication, enable managed identity on App Service and grant RBAC to AI resources for least privilege; restrict resources with private endpoints/firewalls to subscription networks only.
